title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (下集)

topic_alignment.paraphrase: Lee introduces starting over and carrying everything forward as extremes. He gives radar as an example of a component that may serve both a tank and an aircraft.
An unlabeled test input supplies a new adaptation target. Lee describes restarting from the initial model at 1723.054 seconds.
Lee describes passing the adapted model parameters forward to the next input, then asks how to balance the two extremes.
Lee directs students to the previous semester’s lecture 8 for work by his lab on an intermediate design.
Updating model parameters or the harness can impair a past skill. At 1818.416 seconds Lee asks what happens if the agent's harness changes.

topic_alignment.paraphrase: The ASR example introduces adapting to one utterance.
Lee names Dynamic SUTA. Parameters fitted to one input can be unreliable to retain, while more inputs can support a persistent update.
The current utterance gets a temporary fast update. The slow update uses a batch and its parameters are retained for subsequent inputs.
Lee reads the horizontal axis as incoming utterances and the vertical axis as WER change against the unadapted baseline.
Lee mentions automatic model reset and refers listeners to the paper for the mechanism.
